html:
VKF Syntax Reference

1. Programs And Bindings

1.1 Declare With name: And Update With .name:

name: value declares a name; a type may appear before it. .name: value updates the nearest reachable declaration. The leading dot makes accidental creation impossible: .missing: value is a compile error telling you to declare it first with missing:value.

An inner scope may deliberately shadow an outer name with name:. Within one scope, use .name: for every later update. Compound updates follow the same rule; the aggregate examples show them in use. Function parameters already exist in their function scope, so .x +: 3 may update parameter x, while x: 4 in the same scope is a forbidden redeclaration. Module imports are separate: alias: .folder.file has the dotted module path on the right of :.

Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
7
6

Declarations and updates are expressions; each returns the value it stored. The same strict name rule applies inside an expression.

Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
3
4

1.2 Blocks Produce Values And Scopes

An indented block returns its last row. A bare : returns the visible scope as a record.

Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
hello world
make_base(x:3, y:4)
3
red

1.3 Output, Comments, And Assertions

:: value writes a value. condition?! asserts truth. An optional following expression is the error message. # comments through the end of its row. Paired ## ... ## delimit a non-nesting multiline comment; putting such a block first inside a function or nominal constructor is the recommended source-documentation style. The compact ### text## form is therefore ## + comment text beginning with # + ##; it is not a third comment syntax. Comments are absent from runtime artifacts.

Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
42

1.4 Semicolons Preserve Logical Indentation

; ends the current row and begins another at the same logical indentation. Horizontal spaces after the semicolon are ignored. This also works inside an indented pipe stage.

Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
5
[9, 25, 49]

The final bare : returns the block scope so scope.c is available. Without it, the block returns its final row. The direct ret: block evaluates to its final pipeline value without surrounding parentheses.

1.5 Tests And Fixtures

Test files are ordinary VKF files. vkf -t runs every top-level function whose body contains an assertion. Return types do not select tests. Required parameters come from zero-argument functions with the same names; vector fixtures use ordinary VKF lifting. A missing fixture is an error.

Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console


2. Values, Types, And Containers


2.1 Primitive Values And null


The primitive callable type handles are bit, chr, int, num, and str. num also represents complex numbers. A bare @ returns null.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
true
A
1.5
7
null


Primitive names are first-class values of metatype type. Calling one converts a compatible value; postfix . returns the actual type value of any value or callable, rather than a string containing its name. Bare .. remains exclusively the range operator. Primitive type values also expose their members when spilled.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
4
type
[int:2]
TypeScope(reflected:type)


bool, byte, bytes, and float are not primitive names. Use bit, chr, str, num, or a vector of chr values.


2.2 Strings, Characters, And Interpolation


& concatenates text and converts the other operand when needed. Strings compare by content and support $name, $(expression), dotted paths, number formats, and escaped \$. Triple double-quoted and raw triple single-quoted strings span rows. The opening row's leading indentation is removed from continuation rows only if every nonblank row keeps that whole indentation region empty. This also applies when a binding precedes the delimiter, such as text: """first row. Any content inside the indentation region preserves all indentation for the complete literal. Content immediately after the delimiter does not add an initial newline; putting the first content on the next row does.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
Hej världen
value=4.23
sum=5 point=(x:2, y:false) cost=$5
😀
true


2.3 Tuples And Records


Tuples use positional fields. Records use named fields. Read a record field with .field, a literal tuple or vector index with .0, and a computed index with .(index). Update the same selection by placing it on the left of :.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
12
origin
12


2.4 Fixed And Dynamic Vectors


[T:n] is a fixed vector type and [T] is dynamic. Type values use the same forms: [int, int, int] canonicalizes to [int:3], while the one-item [int] denotes the dynamic vector type rather than [int:1]. [any] is an open uniform vector type whose exact element type is inferred when specialized; it never permits heterogeneous elements. A value literal is fixed unless a dynamic type is requested. [value:count] repeats an element.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
[1, 2, 3]
[4, 20, 6]
[7, 7, 7, 7, 9, 9]


& concatenates vectors. Fixed vectors preserve their compile-time shape; dynamic vectors produce a dynamic result.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
[1, 2, 3]
[1, 2, 3]


2.4.1 Multidimensional And Distributed Indexing


vector.(i, j, k) indexes every dimension in one operation. A spilled fixed coordinate vector supplies the same arguments, so vector.(:coordinates) is equivalent to vector.(coordinates.0, coordinates.1, coordinates.2).


Index markers are structural syntax: : preserves one existing dimension, ... preserves all remaining dimensions, and :: reserves a new size-one dimension. A complete preserving index is therefore written as tensor.(...) or tensor.(:, :). Markers compose with fixed or computed indices: tensor.(..., 1) fixes the final dimension, matrix.(row, :) selects one row while preserving its columns, and matrix.(::, :, :) adds a leading size-one dimension.


Vector-valued indices use the ordinary function-application rule. Matching index shapes zip, scalar indices repeat for every selected value, and nested index vectors preserve their nested result shape. The same forms work on the left of : for updates.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
11
11
[1, 13, 21]
[[2, 12], [22, 32]]


This deliberately heavy example performs 10 million fixed-container element updates and reads. It is the runtime stress case in the per-example release report; only its checksum is printed.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
10000000


2.5 Aggregate Updates And Aliases


Compound updates also require the explicit leading dot: .name +:, .name -:, .name *:, .name /:, .name //:, .name %:, and .name /\:. The native implementation preserves aggregate alias identity across these updates. Built-in vector arithmetic distributes over vector elements. Tuple and record arithmetic is never inferred field-by-field; define an operator overload for the complete type instead.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
[3, 4]
(x:5, y:6, name:my point)


The exact output is [3, 4] followed by (x:5, y:6, name:my point). The vector updates are built in; the record update resolves the declared + overload. Both updates remain visible through older aliases of the same aggregate.


2.6 Multisets


{value:count} creates a multiset. Ordinary multiset keys require one exact type. {int} is instead the first-class multiset type whose elements are int; {any} is its open uniform form. Counted type values remain data: {int:3, num:2} counts two different type objects and its reflected type is {type}. This is the only container/type syntax where counts deliberately keep the result as a value rather than constructing a type. Duplicate keys combine and nonpositive counts disappear. + or & adds counts, - subtracts, // divides matching counts, and % keeps remainders.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
{a:7, b:1, c:2}
{a:1, b:1}
{a:2}
{a:1}


2.7 Inclusive Ranges


start..end is an inclusive integer range. Omitting the start uses zero. Descending ranges infer a negative step. Omitting the end creates an infinite range, which must be stopped by its consumer. A bare range remains a range object. Parentheses materialize it as a tuple, [] as a vector, and {} as a multiset. Arithmetic then follows the container rules; for example, [..4] / 4 has type [num:5] and value [0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1].


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
[0, 1, 2, 3]
[3, 2, 1, 0]
(1, 2, 3, 4)


2.8 Complex Numbers


num(real, imaginary) creates a complex number. Arithmetic, powers, equality, ordering, function arguments, and string conversion are native.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
1 + 2i
-3 + 4i


2.9 Equality Has Two Forms


== and != reduce exact aggregate equality to one bit. Single = is semantic and remains element-wise for structures.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
1
1
[1, 1]


2.10 Member Reflection And Spill


Postfix . produces a first-class type value. A structured type can be spilled into another type container: (:Point) exposes a nominal type's backing record type. For a closed record value a, [:a] and [:a.] both return its accessible field names in declaration order as an exact [str:N] vector. Spilling a nominal record type, such as [:Point], returns the same ordered keys. Record key reflection discards field values and never coerces heterogeneous fields to one value type. {:a} and {:a.} return the same keys as a multiset<str>, without an ordering guarantee, while (:a.) retains field-type reflection as a record type value.


This record-specific rule does not change positional type vectors. For example, [:(1, 2, 3).], [int, int, int], and [int:3] remain the same [int:3] type value. Mixed type values such as [int, num] have type [type:2]; they remain type data and do not promote to a numeric vector. A primitive type may also be spilled into scope.


Compatibility note for 0.4.0: [:a.] and [:Point] no longer produce a homogeneous vector type from record field types. Use (:a.) or (:Point) for record field-type reflection.


A string selects a record field structurally: a.(name) returns that one field, where name may be a runtime str. A fixed selector vector distributes in selector order: a.(["x", "label"]) returns a fixed vector when the selected field types have one normal common target, and otherwise returns a tuple. Normal numeric promotion applies, so int and num fields share a num result. This also makes a.([:a]) the explicit declaration-order extraction of unnamed field values. A dynamic selector is accepted only when every accessible field has one statically guaranteed common result type. Real record fields take precedence over an overload of ., while absent literal names retain the existing overload fallback. The overload is __getattr__-like rather than __getattribute__-like: a dynamic selector also reads a real field first and calls the overload only when the key is absent. Its result must share the selector's normal common target type. Repeated fixed keys preserve repeated lanes in exact selector order. Fixed unknown keys are diagnosed before the subject is materialized when no . overload can provide them; otherwise each missing lane uses that fallback.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
(x:int, y:int)
[x, y]
[x, y]
{x:1, y:1}


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
64


3. Functions And Calls


3.1 Definitions, Results, And Early Return


A function body returns its last row. @: returns a value immediately; bare @ returns null.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
7
3
null


3.2 Typed, Default, And Named Arguments


Parameters and results may be typed. Defaults can use earlier parameters. Named arguments bind by name and may be mixed with positional arguments.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
234
345
345


3.3 Local Functions, Recursion, And Closures


Functions may be local. Calling a function's own unqualified name is recursion. A returned local function keeps the values it captured from its defining scope.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
720
7


3.4 Lambdas And Higher-Order Functions


Functions are values and may be passed to typed function parameters. (parameters): expression creates a lambda; it can be called immediately or stored.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
10
25
9


3.5 Variadics And Spreads


...name:type captures remaining positional arguments. :::name captures remaining named arguments. :value at a call site spreads a vector, tuple, or record.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
10
7
(flag:true, mode:fast)


Empty heterogeneous variadics are valid. Call-site spread keeps owned values and structural shapes.


Spread also flattens fixed values inside tuple and vector literals.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
(1, 2, 3, 4)
4


3.6 Compile-Time Shape Parameters


Lowercase names inside fixed vector sizes are inferred compile-time numbers. Size expressions compose in parameter and result types.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]


3.6.1 Named Generic Types And Singleton Tuples


An unbound uppercase type name such as T is a compile-time generic type. The compiler binds it from each call and specializes the complete function body. Repeated occurrences of T must receive one exact type. Generic types compose inside vectors, multisets, tuples, and records; shape names such as n bind independently.


Parentheses group one type, so (num) canonicalizes to num. A one-element tuple requires its trailing comma: (num,). Consequently num->num takes one numeric argument, while num,->num takes one argument whose value is a one-element tuple. A pair domain (num,num)->num takes two arguments; ((num,num))->num takes one tuple argument.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
vkf
4
[int:3]
6


3.6.2 Compile-Time Suffix Parameters


A function may capture characters attached to its call name with a bracketed parameter list between the function name and runtime parameters. For example, L[row:dig, column:dig](x:int) is called as L_03(4); row and column are the integer values 0 and 3 inside the function body. dig accepts one decimal digit, bit accepts 0 or 1, and chr captures one character.


The final suffix parameter may be variadic. _suffix[...args:chr](x:int) called as _suffix_abc(7) receives args as the fixed character list [chr(97), chr(98), chr(99)]. An exact function or binding name takes precedence over suffix capture; otherwise the longest declared base name is used. Uppercase functions with suffix parameters are ordinary functions, not nominal constructors.


3.7 Open any Inference


any is an anonymous compile-time inference hole, not runtime type erasure. Each occurrence may specialize independently. [any] and {any} still require one uniform concrete element type. An any parameter may use fields or fixed indices; the compiler infers the required open shape and ignores unrelated record fields.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
2
7


3.8 Nominal Constructors And Overloads


An uppercase function name defines a nominal type. Its returned value is the type's backing representation and may be a scalar, vector, tuple, record, or local scope. A lowercase function does not create a nominal type; its result retains the type of the value returned by its body, including an existing nominal type.


Functions of either case may share a name when their parameter signatures differ. Exact parameter matches win over compatible conversions. All uppercase overloads with one name construct the same nominal type. Postfix . on an instance returns that nominal type; explicitly spilling a record instance before reflection, (:value)., reveals its structural type. Bare .. remains the range operator. A nominal type itself may be spilled: (:Point) is its backing record type, (:Point). is type, and [:Point] is the declaration-order [str:N] vector of its backing record's accessible field names.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
Point
(x:num, y:num)
(x:num, y:num)
type
[x, y]
true
[int:3]
(x:num, y:num)
integer
number


4. Automatic Vector Function Application


Vector lifting is a core language rule, not a special feature of math. Every compatible parameter participates, whether it is supplied positionally, by name, or beside a defaulted parameter. Scalars broadcast, shared named indices align elementwise, and distinct named indices tensorize. Native and WebAssembly use this same syntax and rule. VKF never searches inside tuples or records for fields to transform.


4.1 Compatible Vector Elements Are Selected


The element type must satisfy the same safe conversion rule as an ordinary scalar call. Nested vectors are traversed recursively and retain their shape.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
[2, 4, 6]
[[2, 4], [6, 8]]


The first call lifts over one vector layer. The second reaches the same int leaf type through two vector layers.


4.2 Safe Scalar Conversions Apply At Every Vector Depth


An int can widen to num in a direct call, so the same widening is allowed when lifting through one or more vector dimensions. Narrowing and unrelated conversions remain errors. Exact leaf overloads outrank converted leaf overloads, and an exact whole-container overload outranks all lifting.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
[4, 1.5, -2]


4.3 Tuples And Records Are Atomic


VKF does not inspect tuple or record fields looking for compatible scalars. A tuple or record may still be the exact element type of a vector, so a function accepting that complete type can lift over a vector of those values.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
[(x:11, y:-8), (x:13, y:-6)]


Calling translate((x:1, y:2)) is one direct record call. Calling translate(points) lifts through the outer vector, then calls translate once per complete record. Calling translate((name:"sample", x:1, y:2)) does not search for the x and y subset.


4.4 Container Functions Can Lift Over Outer Vectors


A function accepting a complete vector row can lift over a matrix when each row has a compatible vector type.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
[3, 7, 11]


4.5 Exact Container Matches Take Priority


If the complete argument matches the declared type, VKF calls the function once. It does not descend. Declare the complete container type whenever whole-container behavior is intended.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
[2, 3, 1]


4.6 Math Uses The Same Vector Rule


Math functions lift recursively through numeric vectors. They do not transform numeric fields hidden inside tuples or records. This includes abs, roots, trigonometry, logs, exponentials, hyperbolic functions, gamma, and erf.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
[[1, 4], [9, 16]]
[[1, 2], [3, 4]]


5. Control Flow And Errors


Compiler errors name the source file, line, and column, then print the source row with a caret under the failing token. Native and browser compilers preserve the same location through parsing and lowering.


5.1 Conditionals


condition? expression runs the expression only when true. An indented suite is allowed. A false conditional expression returns null.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
1
1.#QNAN


5.2 Match Values And Types


value?? selects an arm with =>. Exact values beat type arms. More specific type, intersection, and shape arms beat broader unions or any. The final unlabelled row is the fallback.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
exact three
another integer


Union and intersection patterns use | and &. Record, tuple, and fixed-vector shapes may also be patterns.


5.3 Conditional And Match Loops


condition?> repeats while its condition is true. value??> repeatedly matches a changing value. In both ?? and ??>, the final unlabelled row is the default arm.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
10
2


5.4 Return, Continue, And Break


@: returns a value, @ returns null, @> continues the nearest loop/pipe, and @| breaks it.


The loop in 5.3 demonstrates continue and break. Inside a pipe block, @: returns from that element only, not from the enclosing function.


5.5 Catching Typed Errors


Error("message") constructs an error value; construction alone does not raise. Postfix ! raises the value on its left. A bare error type supplies an empty message, so Error! is shorthand for Error()!. expression!? catches errors raised by that expression. Arms use =>; $ is the caught error. An unmatched error continues outward. Only error types and constructed error values may be raised; 2! and other ordinary-value raises are compile errors.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
specific value


The exact output is specific value. Native errors include the common base Error plus specific types such as AssertionError, IndexError, and ValueError. Use errors: .errors instead when you prefer qualified names such as errors.ValueError.


6. Pipes, Ranges, And $


6.1 Mapping With >>


value >> expression binds each onward value as $. It maps vectors, tuples, dynamic lists, multisets, ranges, and Unicode string characters. A scalar supplies one onward value. Evaluation is eager: every stage runs when the pipe statement is evaluated, even if its result is discarded. A completed finite range pipe materializes a tuple by default; this does not defer its effects.


As the sole unparenthesized value inside a vector or multiset literal, a pipe generates that container. [a >> $] is equivalent to [:a], and {a >> $} is equivalent to {:a}. Parentheses suppress generation: [(a >> $)] is a one-element vector containing the result tuple. The same grouping boundary applies in {}, subject to the multiset's supported key types.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
[2, 4, 6]
(11, 12, 13)
16
ååAA


Multiset pipes preserve multiplicity. String pipes decode characters from UTF-8 and encode their results back to UTF-8.


6.2 Pipe Blocks And Infinite Ranges


A pipe may use an indented block, which runs once for each input like a function. The block's final value becomes $ for the next >> stage. Dotted assignment can update an existing outer binding. @: returns that element's result, @> skips onward, and @| stops consumption, including an infinite range.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
[1, 20, 3, 4]


6.3 Indexed Assignment In A Pipe


An indexed assignment may be a pipe stage. It executes once for each input and its stored value becomes $ for the next stage. $ is a special computed index, so it uses parentheses after the dot.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
[4, 3, 2, 1]
(40, 30, 20, 10)


7. Operators And Overloads


7.1 Built-In Operators


Arithmetic uses + - * / // % ^; concatenation uses &. Logic uses /\ \/ >< ~. Ordering uses < <= > >=; equality uses = == !=.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
14
3
2
256
true
true


/\ and \/ short-circuit. Power binds more tightly than multiplication. Unary - and ~ are supported.


7.2 Absolute Value And Vector Norm


|value| is absolute value for a scalar and Euclidean norm for a numeric vector.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
5
5


7.3 Operator Overloads


Define an operator like a function with custom parameter types. Unary operators and dotted field/index access may also be overloaded.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
(x:4, y:6)
(x:-3, y:-4)


Overloading str(custom) controls conversion and interpolation. Overloading ::(custom) controls direct output.


7.4 Dotted Access Overloads


Overload . to interpret custom field and dotted-index names. Normal record fields remain available inside the overload.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
3
4


8. Shapes, Axes, And Indexing


8.1 Fixed Shapes


Fixed vector shapes nest, survive calls, and compose through compile-time size expressions. Dynamic vectors use [T] and expose runtime storage.


Fixed rectangular vector values expose .shape as a fixed integer vector and .ndim as the scalar integer rank. Shape dimensions run from the outermost vector on the left to the innermost vector on the right: [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]].shape is [2, 3] and its .ndim is 2. Dynamic and jagged vectors do not expose these attributes in this release.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
5


8.2 Single And Multi-Index Access


Use .1 for a literal index. Use .(expression) whenever an index must be evaluated, including a bound name such as index, the pipe value $, a calculation, or multiple indices. A bare .name is literal member access; it never evaluates name. The same indexing syntax followed by : updates the selected positions.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
20
[10, 30]
[10, 21, 30, 41]


Out-of-range dynamic indexing raises errors.IndexError.


8.3 Index Names And Tensor Products


Each character in an attached structural suffix names one ordered vector dimension: _a names a rank-one value, while _aq names the two dimensions of a rank-two value. Parentheses do not add dimensions, so [(1,2),(3,4)]_a is rank one while [[1,2],[3,4]]_aq is rank two.


A suffix normally names the complete vector rank. Use one ... only when anonymous dimensions must remain implicit: _i...k names the outer dimension i, the final dimension k, and as many positional anonymous dimensions as are needed between them. Named and anonymous dimensions never align implicitly. Named dimensions align by identity; anonymous dimensions align only positionally with anonymous dimensions. Shared named dimensions align element-wise; unmatched dimensions broadcast in left order followed by right-only order.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
[[1, 2, 3], [2, 4, 6], [3, 6, 9]]
[4, 10, 18]
[[[15, 18], [20, 24]], [[30, 36], [40, 48]]]
[[2, 6], [6, 12]]


The first result is a 3 x 3 matrix on indices a,b; the second remains a length-three vector on q; the third is rank three on a,b,q. The fourth aligns its shared q dimension and broadcasts its unmatched a dimension.


Index names carry no built-in meaning unless they are one of the deliberately structural names below. Most dimension names are generic grouping/alignment names. Renaming a, b, i, j, k, or q consistently does not change a computation. Seven names have structural meaning: u, v, and w describe connected topology; t describes time; p selects position components; c selects color components; and m is a member/reference slot in explicit topology. For example, p_up is a connected curve, p_uvp is a surface, and edge_bm stores edge-member references while b remains an ordinary edge grouping dimension.


In viewport.add(x:x_i, y:y_i), x and y are property names and the supplied values carry the structural i dimension. The letter i has no built-in plotting meaning. An unindexed container receives an implicit grouping index, but explicit indices are recommended because every dimension remains named.


Coordinate arguments are library-level semantics, but use the same structural suffix vocabulary. The selected suffix axis governs its controls: for stat.sum_q, use q:, q_from, q_to, and q_step; for integ_q, use q:, q_from, q_to, and dq. The suffix letter is substituted directly into each control name. With no coordinate vector, q_step is an integer index stride. Supplying q: changes it into a coordinate-space lattice and sampled values are linearly interpolated at that lattice. Numerical integration instead uses dq for a constant measure; with q: it derives the measure from the supplied coordinates.


Each Layer owns its playback mode. A _t value establishes the time index and defaults to integer sample coordinates; t: or t_min: plus t_max: may replace those coordinates. The four modes are "repeat" (wrap and continue), "mirror" (reverse at each end), "stop" (stay at the last sample), and "reset" (jump to the first sample and stop). Different layers in one view may therefore have different time domains and playback modes.


9. Modules, Scope, And Dispatch


9.1 Module Handles And Imports


.name is a module handle. Bind it to an alias or spill it with :.name. Local .vkf modules use the same import model and are fingerprinted as build dependencies.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
3
1


9.2 Shadowing And Qualification


Local names shadow outer value layouts and unbound builtin module names. A bound module alias qualifies the library explicitly, which is also how a function avoids accidentally calling itself.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
0
4


9.3 Overload Families And Type Dispatch


Multiple functions with the same name form an overload family selected by parameter compatibility. Match arms use the same type-specificity rules.


Run in browser · 0.4.7
Console
integer
text


10. Reading Diagnostics


Most examples on this site complete successfully. The two below intentionally fail and are labelled Expected error. Run them to see the compiler report the file, line, column, failing source row, and exact position.


10.1 Raising Requires An Error Value


Postfix ! raises the value on its left, so that value must be an error.


Run in browser · 0.4.7 · Expected error
Expected diagnostic
<browser>:2:1: `!` expects an error value
value!
^


10.2 A Suffix Must Match The Value's Indices


A reference cannot claim an index that its value does not carry.


Run in browser · 0.4.7 · Expected error
Expected diagnostic
<browser>:2:4: index suffix _ui does not match values axes _u
:: values_ui
   ^


Continue reading


Import and use published modules in the separate Standard Library, or return to the Guide.
